about.lead:
A <m>Nostr</m> conference
from Japan, and a festival.
about.nostrasiaText: Started in 2023, a place where people who build Nostr, use Nostr, or are just curious about it all gather in one spot. There are talks, hands-on sessions, a market, and even a shrine. It continued in 2024 and 2025, and 2026 is planned too.
about.nostrSub: Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays
about.nostrText: A decentralized protocol that doesn't depend on any single company. Your key (npub / nsec) is your account, and your posts (notes) live on multiple relays. Read and write with any client you like, and send a small amount of bitcoin to posts you love with a zap ⚡.

talk.title: Talks & LT
talk.text: People who build and use Nostr talk about where it is now and where it's going.

handson.title: Hands-on
handson.text: From creating your keys to using a client, try it yourself on the spot.

market.title: Market
market.text: A market for the Nostr scene, with zaps ⚡ flying around.

shrine.title: Nostr Shrine
shrine.text: Somehow, it exists. You can pay a visit.

dj.text: DJs and a social space: an offline timeline.

faq.lead: Don't worry. Most people here are <m>new</m> to it.

first.q: Can I come if I've never used Nostr?
first.a: Yes. Past editions have included hands-on sessions and other content for first-timers. The 2026 content is being arranged.

keys.a: npub is your public key (like a business card), and nsec is your private key (like a password). Never show your nsec to anyone.

relay.a: A server that stores and delivers posts (notes). You connect to several relays at once, so one going down doesn't hurt much.

zap.a: A way to send a small amount of bitcoin (Lightning) to a post. A bit more weight than a "like".

nip.a: Nostr Implementation Possibilities: a set of documents describing the Nostr spec, feature by feature. For example, kind:1 is a short text note.

client.title: Pick a client
client.text: Install one app you can use on your phone or in your browser.

keys.title: Make your keys
keys.text: <c>npub</c> is fine to share; keep <c>nsec</c> to yourself.
